column2: Missed dialysis causes hyperkalaemia, first seen as tall tented T waves; give IV calcium, insulin–glucose and urgent dialysis.
Pleuritic pain, haemoptysis and breathlessness on the pill suggest PE, whose commonest ECG finding is sinus tachycardia; confirm with CTPA.
Hypothermia (31 °C) produces J (Osborn) waves at the QRS–ST junction; rewarm gently as the cold heart is prone to VF.
Pain and anxiety after trauma cause sinus tachycardia; persistent tachycardia should prompt a search for occult bleeding.
Pulmonary oedema with a new apical pansystolic murmur 2–7 days after inferior MI is acute MR from posteromedial papillary rupture; urgent echo and surgery.
Fever and pleuritic pain relieved by sitting forward 4 weeks after MI is Dressler syndrome; aspirin/NSAID plus colchicine.
P waves at 90/min unrelated to broad QRS at 40/min is complete heart block; with hypotension give atropine and temporary pacing.
Collapse 2–5 days after anterior MI with hypotension, raised JVP and small QRS complexes is tamponade from free-wall rupture.
Orthopnoea and PND weeks after MI indicate left ventricular failure; echo, diuretics and prognostic HF therapy.
Hypertension with K⁺ 2.2, high-normal sodium and polyuria is Conn's syndrome; aldosterone:renin ratio, then adrenal CT and venous sampling.
Paroxysmal anxiety, palpitations, headache and flushing with hypertension suggest phaeochromocytoma; measure metanephrines, alpha-block first.
Turner syndrome with hypertension and an interscapular systolic murmur is coarctation; check radiofemoral delay.
Hypertension, flank mass and a family history of early brain haemorrhage (berry aneurysm) point to ADPKD; confirm by renal ultrasound.
Hypertension with acne, hirsutism and bruising suggests Cushing's syndrome; screen with overnight dexamethasone suppression, then ACTH.
In acute LVF at fast rates S3 and S4 fuse into one loud extra sound: a summation gallop.
MR gives a pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla; loudness does not reflect severity.
Aortic sclerosis gives an ejection murmur at the right 2nd space without carotid radiation, with a normal pulse and A2.
A large chronic pericardial effusion muffles the heart sounds; look for tamponade signs (pulsus paradoxus, raised JVP).
Severe AR can cause an Austin Flint murmur (apical mid-diastolic rumble from the jet hitting the mitral leaflet), without opening snap.
An irregularly irregular pulse is characteristic of AF; confirm by ECG and assess CHA2DS2-VASc.
Arcus, xanthelasma and tendon xanthomas with premature family CAD is heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (~1 in 250); cascade testing.
Fever, weight loss and splinter haemorrhages suggest subacute bacterial endocarditis; 3 blood cultures and echo.
Bradycardia with intermittent cannon a waves and collapse is complete heart block (Stokes–Adams): permanent pacing.
Acute AR (e.g. type A dissection) causes shock with a short soft diastolic murmur and no wide pulse pressure; needs emergency surgery.
ACE inhibitors (ramipril) cause dry cough in ~10% via bradykinin; switch to an ARB.
Amlodipine causes dose-dependent ankle oedema from precapillary dilatation; it responds poorly to diuretics.
Furosemide causes hypokalaemia, giving U waves, flat T waves and ST depression.
Statins (simvastatin) can cause myositis and rhabdomyolysis, especially with interacting drugs; stop it and check CK.
Streptokinase commonly causes hypotension and allergy (bacterial protein) and must not be reused because of antibodies.
Adrenaline's alpha effect raises aortic diastolic and coronary perfusion pressure; 1 mg IV every 3–5 min.
Amiodarone 300 mg IV after the third shock (150 mg after the fifth) is the standard antiarrhythmic in VF/pVT.
Atropine 500 µg IV (to 3 mg) blocks vagal tone and is first-line for unstable bradycardia; no longer used in asystole/PEA.
Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV suppresses torsades de pointes and corrects hypomagnesaemia.
In hyperkalaemic arrest IV calcium stabilises the myocardium; it does not lower K⁺ (insulin–glucose, dialysis do).
Tearing chest and interscapular pain then a stroke in a hypertensive man suggests dissection into the carotids; CT aortography, no thrombolysis.
Atypical chest pain and palpitations with an apical mid-systolic click is mitral valve prolapse; echo confirms.
Angina on lying flat (decubitus angina) reflects increased venous return and implies severe CAD or LV dysfunction; refer for angiography.
Chest pain and surgical emphysema after forceful vomiting in a drinker is Boerhaave syndrome; CT with water-soluble contrast and surgery.
Crushing pain triggered by hot or cold drinks, partly relieved by GTN, with a normal ECG is diffuse oesophageal spasm.
Sudden death in a young athlete with a murmur louder on standing is HOCM; screen first-degree relatives.
Heavy alcohol use with heart failure, functional MR and AF is alcoholic dilated cardiomyopathy; abstinence may reverse it.
A pedunculated LA mass on the septum with fever and weight loss is atrial myxoma; excise surgically.
Positional pericarditic pain in advanced renal failure is uraemic pericarditis: start or intensify dialysis.
Breathlessness after a febrile viral illness with raised CRP and troponin suggests myocarditis; cardiac MRI and avoid exercise 3–6 months.
Alternating sinus bradycardia and tachycardia in an older patient is sick sinus syndrome; pacemaker if symptomatic.
Tachycardia with severe pain after epidural removal is sinus tachycardia from pain; give analgesia and exclude bleeding or sepsis.
Embolic limb ischaemia with intermittent palpitations but a normal ECG suggests paroxysmal AF; ambulatory monitoring and anticoagulation.
Antipsychotics prolong QT and cause torsades (broad tachycardia with twisting axis): IV magnesium, stop drug, defibrillate if pulseless.
ST elevation ≥ 1 mm in two contiguous inferior leads (II, III, aVF) defines inferior STEMI, an indication for reperfusion.
Primary PCI within 120 min is preferred over fibrinolysis: better patency, fewer reinfarctions, strokes and deaths.
Any previous intracranial haemorrhage is an absolute contraindication to thrombolysis (also ischaemic stroke < 6 months, active bleeding, dissection).
Cyclizine raises SVR and LV filling pressure in MI/heart failure; use metoclopramide as the antiemetic.
Aspirin cut 5-week vascular mortality by ~23% in ISIS-2 (additive to streptokinase); give 300 mg chewed at once.
Sternotomy scar with Coombs-negative anaemia and schistocytes is mechanical haemolysis from a prosthetic valve; echo for paravalvular leak.
Bicuspid aortic valve (1–2%) causes mixed AS/AR presenting in middle age; image the whole aorta.
Apical pansystolic murmur to the axilla in a heavy drinker is functional MR from alcoholic dilated cardiomyopathy.
Bifid P waves (P mitrale) reflect LA enlargement, the hallmark of rheumatic mitral stenosis.
Pulmonary hypertension causes functional TR with a pansystolic murmur, oedema and a tender congested liver.
Tricuspid endocarditis in a drug injector is most often S. aureus; septic pulmonary emboli are common.
Subacute IE on a rheumatic mitral valve after dental work is classically viridans streptococci.
